text:
- [LFCA.2.4] `cached(key)` is the cache-read expression — a sync-intent
  language-level affordance, callable from a `let` RHS and a `where` per
  [LGRA.9.8.2] and [LSTO.4.3.1a]. **It is not gateable at all**, and the reason is that
  the cache is engine-owned ([LSTO.4.7]): every engine has
  one, a read takes no integrator callback, so there is no capability a
  tier could lack.

  The two cache **writes** remain gateable ([LFCA.2.1]), but on policy
  rather than capability — a tier may forbid rules from mutating cache
  state. That asymmetry is the whole of it: writes are a permission,
  reads are not.
